pages.title: Bring discoveries home
pages.text: Blueprints unlock patterns without being consumed. Store them beside a Constructor to make equipment back at base.$(br2)Powersuit blueprints are twice as common as matching finished armor in dungeon caches. Sabre and Lance blueprints are also easier to find than the weapons. You still need the ingredients to craft them.$(br2)Some upgrades are loot-only. Keep room for unfamiliar modules.

pages.title: Alien displays
pages.text: Some city buildings, floating dungeon rooms, huge cube control desks and underground console banks carry displays filled with unreadable alien symbols.$(br2)Sneak-right-click an installed Alien Text Module to recover it, or break its display base to drop it. Its symbols and color survive recovery and can decorate a display at home.$(br2)There is no blueprint or crafting recipe for these modules. They are souvenirs rather than useful readings. Look in newly generated ruins for them.

pages.title: Sort your key cards
pages.text: Soldiers can drop city cards, but permissions vary. Keep door access, storage access and forcefield immunity cards until you have checked them.$(br2)A city name identifies the destination, not every permission.$(br2)The card from the final AI Core is your storage-access reward. Use the Ariente chapter’s Key Cards entry if a lock rejects you.

pages.title: Conquered Overworld spoils
pages.text: The huge cube keeps a Holo Storage Cube beside its central AI Core and forcefield generator. Its 24 reward stacks are spoils from the Overworld: Netherite Ingots, Nether Stars, Ghast Tears, a Totem of Undying, enchanted books and diamond pickaxes, potions and other valuables.$(br2)Defeat the Core Guardian, then break the AI Core for the storage-access card. These trophies do not replenish after collection.
